saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Απολλινάριος επίσκοπος Ραβέννας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: the disciple and follower of the apostle Peter, whom he followed from Antioch to Rome and who ordained him bishop of Ravenna. He is not `apollinaris-mosalitinov`, the twentieth-century Russian monk-martyr. The Greek page adds the names the Romanian source did not: Boniface, a distinguished man of Ravenna, deaf and dumb, whom he healed, and his daughter who had a demon; the patrician Rufinus in Aemilia whose daughter he raised; the shipwreck that put him ashore in Moesia of Thrace; the Christian centurion who let him go from prison; and the seven days he lived after the beating that disfigured him. Its distich sets him beside the day's other Ravenna saint — «Tον Aπολινάριον εκτετμημένον, Έσπευσε Bιτάλιος αυτίκα φθάσαι» — and the corpus keeps that Vitalis as `vitalis-the-martyr-23-july`, upgraded on this same day; the page does not say the two knew each other, so no `related` row is proposed. It gives no year anywhere, so no `dates` are proposed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn.
